title: Italian Game: Evans Gambit
line: White gives a pawn to win time and build the center.

steps.text: The Italian Game, with both bishops out.
Offer the pawn on b2. If the bishop takes it, you gain time to build the center.
steps.after: Engines rate this pawn offer about even, and masters choose it now and then. Black takes the pawn.

steps.text: Attack the bishop with a pawn. It has to move again, and your next pawn move to d4 will be guarded.
Push the pawn in front of your queen two squares, into the center.

also.e1g1: Castling first is also played. This lesson pushes the pawn now.

steps.text: Castle instead of taking back. Your king is safe, and the pawn on d4 can wait.

also.d1b3: The queen move is also played here. This lesson castles.

steps.after: Black is a pawn up, but its king is still in the middle and only two of its pieces are out.

steps.text: Jump the knight forward. Now two of your pieces aim at f7.

also.c3d4: Taking back is also played. This lesson goes for the pawn on f7.

steps.after: Black blocks your bishop with a pawn.

steps.text: Take the pawn that blocks your bishop, to open its line to f7 again.
steps.after: Black takes back with the knight, a slip often made at club level. Masters move the knight forward to attack your bishop.

steps.text: That slip leaves f7 guarded by the king alone. Take on f7 with the knight: a sacrifice, since your queen and rook join with checks.
steps.after: The king takes and is out in the open.

steps.text: Check with the queen. It attacks the king and the knight on d5 at once.
steps.after: Black guards with the queen, but the pinned knight is lost and the king has no shelter.

summary: A pawn for time: White builds the center and castles while Black is busy taking, then hits the weak pawn by the king.
